fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses single-phase equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi rather than the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy.

It attributes embrittlement to grain-boundary segregation and brittle precipitation, whereas the target mechanism involves enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary tips.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including maximum embrittlement near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The proposed 25–100°C thermal cycling is outside the relevant 550–750°C aging window and is unlikely to drive substantial stress-assisted solute migration on ordinary mechanical-test timescales.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response is aligned only at the broad level of testing aging-related toughness loss in an HEA and supplies a controlled comparison, microscopy, mechanical measurements, and an explicit falsification rule. It does not reconstruct the target material, thermal-aging series, structural mediator, fracture mechanism, or characteristic non-monotonic outcome. Although approximately 700°C falls within the target aging interval, treating it as a single segregation-inducing pre-aging condition cannot distinguish the ordering maximum at 600°C from ductility recovery at 750°C. TEM and APT could test the proposed alternative, but the experiment omits the decisive observations of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged FCC/B2 boundaries and does not rule out impurity-driven intergranular embrittlement. The alternative is also weakly supported because no evidence is supplied and the claimed solute migration during 25–100°C cycling is kinetically questionable.
